source.title: Label-Imbalanced and Group-Sensitive Classification under Overparameterization
source.authors: Ganesh Ramachandra Kini; Orestis Paraskevas; Samet Oymak; Christos Thrampoulidis

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no text access problem apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports gradient-descent training dynamics and training accuracy for loss-adjusted networks, directly measuring whether training reaches zero or near-zero error, but it studies imbalanced classification recipes rather than the broad random-initialization benchmark claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results under varied loss adjustments and training durations, plus the linear GMM gradient-descent result where training error is reported as zero after the separability threshold. Table 1's validation accuracies and cited results from other studies are not training-error outcomes and are omitted. Figure 4 values are described in text but only displayed graphically.
record.test_reason: The study measures ResNet-32 training accuracy on long-tailed CIFAR-10 under different loss adjustments and training durations, testing V1 in a new imbalanced-data setting. It is not an original source for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's account of training dynamics is broadly correct. More precisely, multiplicative adjustments determine asymptotic cost-sensitive margins for separable fixed-feature linear models, while suitable additive adjustments can counter their harmful initial effect and accelerate convergence. Deep-network experiments are consistent with this account, but the paper does not prove the same asymptotic result for jointly learned deep features.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates cost-sensitive loss adjustments on imbalanced data, with CIFAR-10 ResNet-32 experiments and linear Gaussian-mixture analyses; it does not reproduce the broad benchmark training claim. CIFAR-10 training uses SGD with momentum and a fixed common initialization across losses, while the synthetic gradient-descent setup does not state initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 training accuracy and time to reach 100% vary with the loss adjustment, additive hyperparameter τ, multiplicative hyperparameter γ, and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient descent achieves zero training error for linear classifiers on synthetic Gaussian mixtures when the feature-to-sample ratio is approximately 0.45 or greater.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear classifiers trained with adjusted logistic losses can interpolate sufficiently separable Gaussian-mixture training data.

record.problems: CIFAR-10 training curves are figure-only for several conditions; the text gives no exact 300-epoch training accuracies. The main CIFAR-10 comparison uses validation tuning, and the paper states that more sophisticated tuning and test-set assessment are future work. The text does not state random initialization, and does not report CIFAR-100 training error.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports balanced validation accuracy, not training error. Group-sensitive Waterbirds tables report subgroup and balanced accuracies, not training classification error; these outcomes do not directly measure V1. Cited results from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100 training error, random or corrupted labels, model-size comparisons, Adam, and systematic early-stopping or regularization comparisons are untested. The initialization distribution is not specified; common seeded initial weights across losses are reported.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation and interventions using identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, curvature reduction and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions and interpretations but no readable Figure 4 curves. Near-interpolation verdicts therefore rely on explicit textual descriptions, not reconstructed percentages. Finite-budget shortfalls do not establish persistent optimization failure.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100 training error, random or corrupted labels, model-size sweeps, Adam, smaller models, early stopping generally, or the claim's unqualified random-initialization recipe. CIFAR-10 runs use ResNet-32 with a stated common initialization across losses; the linear synthetic experiment does not state initialization.
The study does not test teacher-student ReLU networks or width effects on spurious local minima.
The study does not compare network depth or identity shortcuts as an intervention on training error.
The study does not compare initializations or measure trainable depth as a function of initialization.
The study does not test learning rates above a stability limit or measure curvature/sharpness dynamics.
The study does not compare batch normalization with no normalization as an intervention on training speed.

rows.note: The text reports the condition and zero training error, but does not assign this statement to individual loss curves.
rows.check: The zero-error finding is correctly reported, but concerns a linear classifier on synthetic Gaussian mixtures, outside V1's convolutional-network and CIFAR scope. Section 3.1 lists CDT, LDAM and LA for Figure 2(a); VS should not be included in this row's operation.

rows.subject: ResNet-32
rows.operation_detail: Train with CDT-loss; vary multiplicative adjustment hyperparameter γ

conditions.value: larger γ values correspond to more dispersed Δy values

rows.note: The authors state that larger γ hurts training performance and delays reaching TPT; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The text establishes impaired training and delayed interpolation for larger gamma, but the row aggregates different hyperparameters with unreadable numerical endpoints. Restrict the partial state to the larger-gamma conditions described as impaired.

source_check.correct: Use cannot_determine for this aggregated figure-only row: the text establishes slower training and delayed interpolation, but gives no endpoints for the varying gamma settings. Partial fitting is explicitly established separately for gamma = 0.15 at epoch 200.

source_check.problem: Delayed interpolation alone does not establish incomplete endpoint fitting across the aggregated gamma settings.
